character_ramp_why: the sheet is quantised through this 11-colour subset of the declared palette, so all four facings share one outfit by construction - four independent generations otherwise returned four different characters (measured 2026-10-16)
note: The idle and sleep columns are direct FLUX outputs; the walk and typing columns are deterministic pixel derivations of the same base (leg/arm region shifts + torso bob), recorded per frame under `derivation`. The char_up / char_right / char_sleep bases are REFERENCE EDITS of char_down (klein's unified generate+edit mode, conditioning image = our own char_down.keyed.png), which is what holds one identity across the facings; no upstream or LimeZu pixels are involved anywhere. SOU-187 (character v2): the wardrobe is the owner-signed-off orange hoodie (#f0872b, shadow #b35d16, highlight #ffc46a) over denim jeans (#44618a) and cream trainers (#f4ead2), the figure is a chibi with the head at ~40% of the 48px frame, and every derived frame keeps its base's pixels as an underlay so no vacated (floor-coloured) pixel can appear - asserted per frame by scripts/v3/check_v3_assets.py, section DERIVED FRAME INTEGRITY. The walk remains a stride, not a hand-drawn cycle.
